title: Collatz KLGrid: advanced-term growth by induction over actual roots
notes: Source inspected 22 September 2026. KLGrid.growth_root uses a 1/50 grid and the natural measure 10*t+floor(log2(a^498)) to retain the advanced term in the positive 3x+1 counting inequalities, avoiding elimination inside class infima. Its roots are at least 3, fertile, and reach 8; a positive bounded certificate is an explicit premise. The table and method are MIT licensed, copyright M. Sharpe 2026. We have not rebuilt the external repository or independently checked its advertised large density certificates. Local adaptation: Problems.Collatz.PreimageGrid independently compiles actual signed tree-count recurrences for nonperiodic fertile minus-map roots a>=4096. The strict inequalities 8193*C(t+29)<=12288*C(t), 16386*C(t)<=12288*C(t+21), and 2^291*8193^498<12288^498 absorb the plus-one in the inverse numerator, preserving measure drops 4, 3, 1. PreimageDomain.lean now supplies a closed domain for every positive target prime to 3, including cycle targets, using a finite orbit barrier and a large nonperiodic ancestor. The signed growth induction is now compiled in PreimageGrowth.lean. An independently generated 177147-row level-12 integer certificate at rate 5059/5000 has been checked entirely by the Lean kernel. PreimageCertificate12.ancestor_density_21_25 proves the eventual X^21<=ancestorCount(a,X)^25 bound for every positive target prime to 3, after exact dyadic interpolation. The external advertised large certificates have still not been independently audited here. No Juggler termination theorem follows. This is an adaptation of the source's root-induction method, not an independent priority claim for that method. The complete MIT notice is retained in the local Lean module.
